en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Covering the Rice.
At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, out of a desire for more, covered the soup or the curry with rice...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not cover the soup or the curry with rice out of a desire for more.
One must not cover the soup or the curry with rice out of a desire for more.
If, out of disrespect and with the desire for more, one covers over the soup or the curry with rice, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
If, through lack of mindfulness or without knowing,
the owners give [the goods] while concealing them, [it is not an offense].
Not out of a desire for more,
"For one who is a first offender.
The sixth training rule is concluded.
